nodes.summary: If an integer sequence $s$ is C-finite, then there are a shift $q \in \mathbb{N}$, an order $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and integers $c_0, \dots, c_{p-1}$ such that the shifted sequence $t(n) = s(n + q)$ satisfies $t(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, t(n + i)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: A tail of a C-finite sequence satisfies a linear recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $c_0, \dots, c_{p-1}$ be integers. If an integer sequence $s$ satisfies $s(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, s(n + i)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, then $s$ is C-finite.
nodes.title: Solutions of linear recurrences are C-finite

nodes.summary: An integer sequence $s \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ is C-finite if there are $p, q \in \mathbb{N}$ and integers $c_0, \dots, c_{p-1}$ such that $s(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, s(n + i)$ for every $n \ge q$.
nodes.title: C-finite integer sequences

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be an integer sequence, let $p, q \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $c_0, \dots, c_{p-1}$ be integers. If $s(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, s(n + i)$ for every $n \ge q$, then the shifted sequence $t(n) = s(n + q)$ satisfies $t(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, t(n + i)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Discarding the exceptional prefix of a C-finite recurrence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
